```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Everything brandkit does starts from one file, `_brand.yml`. This article
covers what goes in it, how to make one with the configurator, the two
dialects it comes in, and how to read it back from R.

## The brand file

brandkit reads and extends the [brand.yml](https://posit-dev.github.io/brand-yml/)
specification. A complete file:

```yaml
meta:
  name: My Brand
color:
  primary: "#2c3e50"
  secondary: "#1abc9c"
  success: "#27ae60"
  danger: "#e74c3c"
  warning: "#f39c12"
  info: "#2980b9"
  light: "#ecf0f1"          # background in light mode
  dark: "#1a252f"           # foreground in light mode
  foreground: "#1a252f"
  background: "#ecf0f1"
color-dark:                 # dark mode (bslib dialect, see below)
  primary: "#5a8a9f"
  secondary: "#4edfc0"
  background: "#121a20"
  foreground: "#e8eff5"
  # ... the rest of the colours, as above
typography:
  fonts:
    - family: Inter
      source: google        # "google", or "file" for local .ttf files
    - family: Montserrat
      source: google
  base:
    family: Inter
    size: 1rem
    line-height: 1.65
    weight: 400
  headings:
    family: Montserrat
    weight: 700
logo:
  small: "logo/brand.png"
  medium: "logo/brand.png"
  large: "logo/brand.png"
defaults:
  bootstrap:
    defaults:               # Bootstrap Sass variables
      border-radius: "0.75rem"
```

A few details worth knowing:

- The `logo:` section uses `small`, `medium` and `large` (not `light`/`dark`).
- A font entry with no `source:` is a Google font, as in Quarto.
  `source: file` needs the `.ttf` files listed under `files:`.
- Optional `meta:` keys: `ornament-label` and `ornament-label-corner`, for
  the text on the corner ornaments (see `vignette("pdf-and-posters")`).

## Make one with the configurator

```{r}
library(brandkit)
configure_brand()
```

This opens a Shiny app with colour presets, font pairings, logo upload and a
live preview. Saving writes `_brand.yml` (and any logo) to the project and
closes the app.

```{r}
configure_brand(path = ".")                     # opens on the brand already there
configure_brand(path = ".", reset = TRUE)       # ignore it, start from defaults
configure_brand(path = ".", format = "quarto")  # preselect the output format
```

**Starting from an existing brand.** If `path` already holds a `_brand.yml`,
every input opens on its current values (colours, font pairing, sizes, border
radius, name, logo), so adjusting a configured project is a nudge rather than
a new run. The preset and font-pairing menus land on the matching entry, or on
*Custom* for a hand-tuned brand.

Things the app has no control for are carried through, not dropped: a named
`color.palette`, and font definitions for local (`source: file`) families. The
one thing not preserved is hand-edited dark colours: the dark palette is
always derived from the light one (the "Auto-generate dark mode palette"
box, which starts ticked whenever the file has dark colours).

**Presets and fonts.** There are 12 colour presets, from *Corporate Navy* and
*Slate & Teal* to *Mint & Peach*, and 10 font pairings plus *Custom*. Every
family offered survives the Typst/PDF path (a bold and an italic face, and a
name that matches what Typst downloads); if you type a custom family in, see
the troubleshooting article for how to check yours.

## Two dialects, one filename

bslib (Shiny) and Quarto read the same file name but disagree about how dark
colours are written, and each rejects the other's form:

| | Shiny / bslib | Quarto |
|---|---|---|
| Dark colours | separate `color-dark:` section | nested `light:` / `dark:` values per colour |
| Bootstrap variables | `defaults: bootstrap: defaults:` | `defaults: bootstrap: defaults:` |
| Read by | bslib | Quarto **and** bslib |

You rarely have to think about this:

- `configure_brand()` has an **Output format** toggle that picks the dialect to
  write. It starts on the format of the file already in `path`.
- Every `create_brand_*()` scaffold writes the dialect its target needs, and
  converts a file in the wrong one regardless of `overwrite`.
- A directory serving both a Shiny app and a Quarto document needs one format
  chosen on purpose, since each scaffold converts the file to its own.

brandkit's own functions read either dialect.

## Reading the brand from R

brandkit parses `_brand.yml` when the package loads (the one found by walking
up from the working directory, or the default brand bundled in the package)
and caches it. Everything else reads from the cache.

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `brand_init(path)` | (re)loads a specific `_brand.yml` into the cache |
| `brand_colors(mode)` | named list of colours, for `"light"` or `"dark"` |
| `brand_fonts()` | list with `base`, `heading`, `all` and `raw` |
| `brand_logo(size)` | resolved path to the logo, or `NULL` |
| `brand_logo_tag(height)` | an inline `<img>` tag for Shiny titles |
| `brand_raw()` | the full parsed YAML, as an escape hatch |

```{r}
brand_init("path/to/_brand.yml")
brand_colors("dark")$primary
```

Fonts are registered for ggplot2 and base graphics through `sysfonts` and
`showtext` when both are installed. Google fonts are downloaded, so the first
load needs a network connection; set `options(brandkit.register_fonts = FALSE)`
before loading to skip it.
